clue.text: Fear not, it paid extravagantly!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Fear not, it paid extravagantly!' (11): the anagram fodder NOT IT PAID has nine letters and lacks the R and E the eleven-letter answer needs; the text looks garbled (perhaps 'not I tip dare') and no source gives the printed clue.

clue.text: Ancient symbols incur damage

definitions.note: the clue gives a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective describing such old carved letters

indicators.note: damage used as a verb tells us to wreck the order of the word before it

explanation.surface: Defacing old carved inscriptions brings penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges INCUR. The definition is loose: the answer describes the ancient symbols rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were the letters of the old Germanic and Norse alphabets, so the adjective covers those ancient characters.

clue.text: Spend time in transit

parts.note: to spend time is to pass it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spends hours travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend time' reads as a single idea, but it splits into two pieces, and 'in' only links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey or crossing from one place to another, which is what transit means.

clue.text: Editor upheld tactic to redistribute in one area

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the letters for editor are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a ploy is a tactic or stratagem

explanation.surface: An editor backs a scheme to reorganise one department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' sounds like a ruling in favour, but in a down clue it turns ED upwards to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy troops or resources is to spread and position them where they are needed in a chosen area.

clue.text: Guys depend on their support

parts.note: guys here are the ropes holding up a tent, not men, and what anchors those ropes in the ground

explanation.surface: Men rely on someone backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like men, but it means guy ropes, which are staked into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent pegs are the stakes driven into the ground to hold a tent's guy ropes taut.

clue.text: After a short month possibly save a lot of notes

indicators.note: after says the scrambled letters come behind the short month in the answer

parts.note: OCT is the short form of October

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word save may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to save a lot of money once a brief month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged letters behind the short month; 'possibly' makes the anagram. 'a lot of notes' sounds like banknotes from saving, but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave spans eight notes of the scale, so several of them cover a great many musical notes.

clue.text: Wild first-night parties — actor may be put off

indicators.note: wild describes disorder, so the following letters are thrown into a new order
first attached to night asks for only that word's opening letter

explanation.surface: After riotous opening-night celebrations, a performer might be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges N (first of 'night') with PARTIES and ACTOR. 'may be' is a link, and 'put off' looks like 'discouraged' but means 'delay'.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to postpone or delay doing something.

clue.text: Girl placed in jail, having used money unwisely

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
pent means shut in or confined, as in pent up

explanation.surface: A young woman is locked up after wasting cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed in jail' looks like a container instruction, but it is one word meaning confined (as in pent-up feelings), simply placed after the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent describes money or time squandered or wasted on the wrong things.

clue.text: Mistrust legal moves to expose these analysts

indicators.note: moves tells us the letters of the two words are shifted around

explanation.surface: Lawyers' manoeuvres reveal people who distrust them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges MISTRUST LEGAL; 'to expose' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgists study and analyse metals and alloys, testing their composition and properties.

clue.text: Makes a circuit round India, New Guinea and Sarawak initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the listed words

explanation.surface: A traveller loops past India, New Guinea and Sarawak in Borneo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is not a link here: its first letter is the first of the five.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to go around it or encircle it.

clue.text: Secures some offal — maybe suiting the men

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or secure
tripe is a kind of offal, the stomach lining of cattle

explanation.surface: A butcher fastens up offal, perhaps the dinner the men like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the definition as an example: pinstripe is one kind of suiting fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a cloth with fine stripes, traditionally made up into business suits for men.

clue.text: Bird, upon a bird's retreat, is exultant

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Bird, upon a bird's retreat, is exultant' (4-1-4): COCK + A + HOOP is plain, but no reading of 'bird's retreat' gives HOOP (no reversal or shelter word fits), so the text may be misread and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bird, upon a bird's retreat, is exultant

clue.text: By way of a way in prospect

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for way goes inside the word for by way of

parts.note: via means by way of
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A view seen while travelling along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view or outlook, the same as a prospect over a landscape.

clue.text: Corner at head of river for him?

definitions.text: Corner at head of river for him?

parts.note: an angle is a corner

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of river

explanation.surface: A spot in the bend near a river's source suits a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a fisherman claiming a spot on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with rod and line, often from a quiet bend of a river.

clue.text: Flashing, with tiling replacement no good!

indicators.note: replacement tells us the letters of tiling are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone moans that the new tiles are a botched job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges TILING into GLINTI. 'Flashing' looks like roofing material in the tiling scene but is the verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glinting gives off brief sparkles of light, as a flashing thing does.

clue.text: Delicate china destined to be cracked?

definitions.meaning: ... porcelain is very thin, translucent china
the covering of an egg is always broken open in the end

explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is very thin fine ware, and an egg's shell is cracked before the egg is cooked or hatched.

clue.text: Green cormorant heading for bay tree

parts.note: a shag is the European green cormorant
a dog's bay is its bark

explanation.surface: A seabird flies towards a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for bay' looks like the first letter of bay, but 'heading for' is a link and 'bay' gives BARK.
explanation.definitionFit: The shagbark is a North American hickory with shaggy, peeling bark.

clue.text: It's dusk, when some people from Ghana touch down

parts.note: the Twi are a people of Ghana, speakers of the Twi language
to light on something is to land or settle on it

explanation.surface: At nightfall, travellers from Ghana land at the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touch down' is LIGHT in the sense of alight or settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim light just after sunset, the same as dusk.

clue.text: Aim to stop crude application of paint in this way

definitions.text: application of paint in this way

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are roughly reshaped

explanation.surface: A painter tries to stop slapping paint on so roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges AIM and STOP; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying paint on thickly so the brush or knife marks show.

clue.text: Basic requirement by the Queen's marshal

parts.note: a must is something essential
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An essential need is met by the royal officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshal' looks like a noun (an officer) but is the verb: to gather troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To muster troops is to assemble or gather them, as a commander marshals forces.

clue.text: In high dudgeon turn and grab me roughly

parts.note: U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

indicators.note: roughly signals that the letters of the words are rearranged in a rough way

explanation.surface: An angry person spins round and seizes the speaker roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges the two words after the U of a U-turn. 'In' is a link: someone in high dudgeon has taken offence, and the noun names that offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrage is resentment or offence, which is what high dudgeon expresses.

clue.text: Off-course, then was stranded

indicators.note: off means not as it should be, so the letters of course are put out of order

explanation.surface: A ship drifted from its route and was then grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges COURSE. Defoe's Robinson Crusoe was shipwrecked and lived alone on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe, Defoe's castaway, spent years marooned on a desert island.

clue.text: Don's laid back — still in bed

indicators.note: laid back tells us the phrase meaning don is read in reverse

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A relaxed university lecturer is having a lie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but it is the verb to put on, and the 's is is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not up has not yet risen and remains in bed.

clue.text: Soldier hugging a bawdy Italian hero

indicators.note: hugging means the letters for soldier wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means bawdy or coarsely humorous

explanation.surface: A soldier embraces a rude Italian champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight for Italian unification in the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi was the general who led the Redshirts in the unification of Italy and is revered as a national hero.

clue.text: Beast a large beetle upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall, like a maul, is a heavy wooden mallet, and a beetle is such a mallet

explanation.surface: An animal knocked over a big insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetle' is not an insect but a heavy mallet. 'upset' turns A MALL upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal of the camel family, kept for wool and as a pack animal.

clue.text: Aunt is in trouble with Pole and other foreign nationals

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters of the three words are disordered

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole

explanation.surface: An aunt has difficulties with a Polish person and other people from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like the anagram signal, but 'in' is part of the letters rearranged; 'Pole' is S, the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisians are citizens of Tunisia, people of another nation from the solver's point of view.

clue.text: Aside made by one character in a play

parts.note: a means one
a part is a role or character in a play

explanation.surface: An actor speaks a stage aside in character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aside' looks like the theatrical whisper in the play scene, but it means to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means to one side or separately, the adverbial sense of aside.

clue.text: Explorer takes military leader for a domestic worker

parts.note: Captain James Cook was the British explorer of the Pacific
a general is a senior army commander

explanation.surface: A navigator swaps his army commander for a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: A cook-general was a servant who did both cooking and general housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook-general was a household servant combining cooking with general housework.
